note: Section sets per page type for saas-landing-builder. House guidance written for this toolkit, not a benchmark: a slot is a job the page must do, and any of its labels fills it. references/page-types.md explains each set in prose and must list the same page type ids; references/section-labels.md defines every label.

labels.hero: First block with the main headline (usually the H1), subheadline and primary CTA.
labels.social_proof: Logo bar, customer counts, ratings, awards or press, without a named person's quote.
labels.problem: Names the pain, cost or status quo the visitor lives with today.
labels.solution: Short answer to the problem: what the product is and the outcome it gives.
labels.features: Benefit-led capability blocks or a feature grid.
labels.how_it_works: Numbered steps from start to outcome, or what happens after the CTA.
labels.product_demo: Interactive demo, video walkthrough or click-through product tour.
labels.testimonials: Named quotes, case studies or customer stories tied to a person or company.
labels.pricing: Plans and prices, a plan comparison table, or a pricing teaser that links to the pricing page.
labels.faq: Questions and answers, usually an accordion, that handle objections.
labels.integrations: Tools the product connects with, the API, or the ecosystem it fits into.
labels.security: Security, compliance, privacy or reliability proof (for example SOC 2, GDPR, uptime).
labels.comparison: Side-by-side with alternatives or the old way of doing the job.
labels.use_cases: Blocks by role, team, industry or job to be done.
labels.final_cta: Closing block whose main job is the conversion ask, near the end of the page.
labels.lead_form: An inline form on the page (demo request, waitlist, contact).
labels.footer: Site footer, labelled from the chrome facts: legal links, navigation, contact.
labels.other: Anything else: changelog, blog or event teasers, careers, newsletter, announcements.
